sq.ANSWER:
#include <iostream>

using namespace std;

 

struct Student {

    int id;

    string name;

    Student* prev;

    Student* next;

};

 

// Function to delete a student by ID

void deleteFromMiddle(Student*& head, int targetID) {

    if (head == nullptr) {

        cout << "List is empty.\n";

        return;

    }

 

    Student* temp = head;

 

    // Traverse to find the node

    while (temp != nullptr && temp->id != targetID) {

        temp = temp->next;

    }

 

    if (temp == nullptr) {

        cout << "Student ID " << targetID << " not found.\n";

        return;

    }

 

    // Cannot delete head or tail using this middle function

    if (temp == head || temp->next == nullptr) {

        cout << "Cannot delete head or tail using this function.\n";

        return;

    }

 

    // Adjust links to bypass the node

    temp->prev->next = temp->next;

    temp->next->prev = temp->prev;

 

    delete temp;

    cout << "Student ID " << targetID << " deleted from the middle.\n";

}

#include <iostream>

using namespace std;

 

struct Guest {

    int id;

    string name;

    Guest* prev;

    Guest* next;

};

 

// Function to delete the last node

void deleteAtEnd(Guest*& head) {

    if (head == nullptr) {

        cout << "List is empty.\n";

        return;

    }

 

    // Case 1: Only one node in the list

    if (head->next == nullptr) {

        delete head;

        head = nullptr;

        cout << "Last guest record deleted. List is now empty.\n";

        return;

    }

 

    // Case 2: More than one node

    Guest* temp = head;

    while (temp->next != nullptr) {

        temp = temp->next;

    }

 

    temp->prev->next = nullptr;

    delete temp;

 

    cout << "Last guest record deleted.\n";

}
sq.QUESTION_DESC:
In a hotel management system, guest check-out details are stored in a doubly linked list, where each node contains the guest ID and guest name. When a guest checks out, their record (the last node) must be deleted from the list.

Write a function in C++ to delete the last node (i.e., perform deletion at the end) of the doubly linked list.

lq.ANSWER:
#include <stdio.h>

#include <stdlib.h>

 

// Node structure representing a customer

struct Customer {

    int tokenNo;

    struct Customer* prev;

    struct Customer* next;

};

 

// Insert at end (setup function)

void insertAtEnd(struct Customer** head, int token) {

    struct Customer* newNode = (struct Customer*)malloc(sizeof(struct Customer));

    newNode->tokenNo = token;

    newNode->next = NULL;

 

    if (*head == NULL) {

        newNode->prev = NULL;

        *head = newNode;

        return;

    }

 

    struct Customer* temp = *head;

    while (temp->next != NULL)

        temp = temp->next;

 

    temp->next = newNode;

    newNode->prev = temp;

}

 

// Delete from beginning

void deleteFromBeginning(struct Customer** head) {

    if (*head == NULL) {

        printf("Queue is empty.\n");

        return;

    }

 

    struct Customer* temp = *head;

    printf("Customer with token %d served (deleted from front).\n", temp->tokenNo);

 

    *head = (*head)->next;

 

    if (*head != NULL)

        (*head)->prev = NULL;

 

    free(temp);

}

 

// Delete from end

void deleteFromEnd(struct Customer** head) {

    if (*head == NULL) {

        printf("Queue is empty.\n");

        return;

    }

 

    struct Customer* temp = *head;

 

    // Only one customer

    if (temp->next == NULL) {

        printf("Customer with token %d left the queue (deleted from end).\n", temp->tokenNo);

        free(temp);

        *head = NULL;

        return;

    }

 

    while (temp->next != NULL)

        temp = temp->next;

 

    printf("Customer with token %d left the queue (deleted from end).\n", temp->tokenNo);

    temp->prev->next = NULL;

    free(temp);

}

 

// Display queue

void displayQueue(struct Customer* head) {

    if (head == NULL) {

        printf("Queue is empty.\n");

        return;

    }

 

    printf("Current Queue (Front to End): ");

    while (head != NULL) {

        printf("[%d] <-> ", head->tokenNo);

        head = head->next;

    }

    printf("NULL\n");

}

 

// Main

int main() {

    struct Customer* queue = NULL;

 

    // Adding customers to queue

    insertAtEnd(&queue, 101);

    insertAtEnd(&queue, 102);

    insertAtEnd(&queue, 103);

    insertAtEnd(&queue, 104);

 

    displayQueue(queue);

 

    // Serve the first customer

    deleteFromBeginning(&queue);

    displayQueue(queue);

 

    // Last customer cancels

    deleteFromEnd(&queue);

    displayQueue(queue);

 

    return 0;

}

ADVANTAGES:

  • Allows quick deletion from both front and end — essential for queues with exits on both sides.
  • Supports bidirectional traversal, useful for monitoring and reporting.
  • More flexible than singly linked lists for applications where nodes can leave from either end.
